questions.explain: The bucket allows bursts while enforcing a sustained rate; lazy refill computes accrued tokens at consume time (no background job); the single-statement UPDATE…WHERE…OUTPUT is atomic so concurrent requests cannot overspend.
options: Fixed window counters
Token bucket with lazy refill and single-statement atomic consumption
No rate limiting; rely on quotas
Application-level sleep calls

questions.explain: Three windows tracked simultaneously with MERGE-based atomic increments: per-minute (abuse), per-day (fair use), per-month (billing) — each serving a different purpose.
options: Only a monthly quota is needed
Only per-minute limits
Track one window at a time
Minute, day, and month windows simultaneously via atomic MERGE, serving abuse, fair-use, and billing purposes

questions.explain: Not all tokens cost the same — weights (e.g., chat_output 4.0 vs. embedding 0.05 per 1k) make one quota unit equal one cost unit; weights are versioned for invoice disputes and updated when provider pricing changes.
options: Weight consumption by feature cost so one quota unit equals one cost unit; version weights for disputes
Charge all features equally
Quotas don't need cost weighting
Weight by token count only

questions.explain: Rate limits return HTTP 429 with Retry-After and X-RateLimit-Remaining; exhausted monthly quotas return HTTP 402 with an upgrade URL; agents get structured {limited, retry_after_s} signals; a quota-status UI prevents surprises.
options: Return 500 for everything
429 + Retry-After for rate limits, 402 + upgrade URL for quota exhaustion, structured signals for agents
Never tell users about limits
Use the same code for all limit types

questions.explain: Grace periods allow a configurable overage (e.g., 10%, invoiced) and borrowing records negative carryover — but grace is a billing feature, never extended to the per-minute abuse bucket, which stays absolute.

Grace overage and borrowing for monthly quotas, but never for the per-minute abuse bucket
Unlimited grace for all limits
